scope: V2 Student architecture selection, hyperparameter tuning, and inner-CV evaluation only. Final V2 protocol frozen separately after selection.
supersedes_note: Does NOT supersede V1 Student protocol. V1 remains the frozen baseline. V2 is a new development track.
design_constraint: All V1 Teacher/label/fold/route constraints remain binding. V2 changes only Student architecture and training objectives.

confirmed_failures.evidence: R1d event-boundary reset yields +0.10 to +0.30 later-event recall; even first events gain +0.17 to +0.23; random reset hurts
R1c train AUROC 0.93 vs val AUROC 0.72; short-event gap 0.44; long-event gap 0.01
R1b missed events mean 23 steps vs detected 55 steps; R1c short-dur train recall only 0.63-0.77
25D9D vs 25D: grasp -0.001, manipulation -0.002, release +0.046; all other metrics near-identical

confirmed_non_failures.evidence: R1e logistic probe AUROC 0.837 (identity-CV), closure_score single-feature 0.831
Simple LR on 25D features achieves higher OOF AUROC than V1 GRU
macro recall 0.92, train and OOF both strong

v1_failure_diagnosis.key_gap: Simple logistic regression (AUROC 0.837) outperforms V1 GRU Student (AUROC 0.717) on held-out identities. The problem is not missing information — it is the Student architecture that fails to generalize the available information.

core_design_principles: Bounded temporal context — no persistent state across the full episode
Fixed-length causal window — eliminates implicit step-index and episode-length shortcuts
Event-balanced training — short events get comparable weight to long events
Identity-balanced training — each identity contributes comparable gradient
25D as primary model — 9D policy intent as pre-registered incremental ablation only
Simple linear baseline — V2 Student must demonstrably beat identity-CV logistic regression

candidate_a.encoder: causal TCN (temporal convolution network with causal padding)
candidate_a.description: Fixed receptive field TCN. No hidden state carried across steps. Each step prediction uses only the past W steps of 25D features.
candidate_a.loss: masked step BCE per head (same as V1)
candidate_a.route_heads: unchanged from V1 (single + multi factorized heads)

candidate_b.description: Same TCN encoder as V2A but with event-balanced release loss + event-level MIL auxiliary objective.

loss.release_event_balance: each release event contributes equal weight regardless of duration; background negative steps batched separately
loss.release_top_k_aux: top-k mean (k=3 pre-frozen) of release probabilities within each Teacher release event known-mask region, trained with BCE against event-positive label

candidate_c.encoder: windowed GRU — GRU cell re-initialized from zero every W steps
candidate_c.description: GRU with periodic hidden state reset. Within each window, state evolves normally. At window boundaries, hidden state is zeroed. No state crosses window boundaries.
candidate_c.window_reset: hard zero every W steps; no learned reset gate; no overlap between windows
candidate_c.loss: same event-balanced + top-k auxiliary as V2B

candidate_d.encoder: best 25D architecture from {V2A, V2B, V2C} + 9D fusion
candidate_d.description: Take the winning 25D-only architecture. Add 9D policy-intent features via a secondary bounded-context encoder. Fuse late (after temporal encoding).
candidate_d.fusion: late fusion: 25D temporal features + 9D temporal features concatenated before route heads
candidate_d.9d_encoder: same architecture type as 25D encoder (TCN or windowed GRU), separately parameterized
candidate_d.ablation_requirement: must compare against: (a) real 9D, (b) shuffled 9D (permuted across episodes), (c) zero 9D. Real 9D must beat both.

selection_rules.description: Candidates are compared in strict priority order. A candidate that fails a higher-priority criterion is eliminated regardless of lower-priority performance.
selection_rules.data_split: V2 inner development uses identity-level cross-validation within the V1 training folds. V1 OOF validation identities are HELD OUT from all V2 development.

criteria.name: safety_upper_bounds
criteria.description: Eliminate any candidate whose best hyperparameter configuration exceeds ANY of: unsupported_route_emit > 0, background_false_emit_rate > 0.10, release_overlap_emit_rate > 0.05.
criteria.measurement: inner-CV pooled across folds; worst-case across seeds

criteria.name: release_auprc_identity_cv
criteria.description: Maximize release event AUPRC (area under precision-recall curve) in identity-level cross-validation. AUPRC is preferred over AUROC due to positive class imbalance.
criteria.measurement: mean AUPRC across inner-CV folds; per-route breakdown required

criteria.name: short_event_auprc
criteria.description: Maximize release AUPRC on events with duration < 30 steps. This is the primary V1 failure region.
criteria.measurement: mean AUPRC on events ≤ 30 steps across inner-CV folds

criteria.name: first_later_event_gap
criteria.description: Minimize |later_event_recall - first_event_recall| at CAL-determined threshold. Large gap indicates residual state pollution.
criteria.measurement: absolute difference between first and later event recall

criteria.name: parameter_efficiency
criteria.description: If candidates are statistically indistinguishable on criteria 1-4, select the one with fewer parameters.

selection_rules.baseline_requirement: Selected V2 candidate must achieve release AUPRC (identity-CV) > simple logistic regression baseline (AUROC 0.837 equivalent). If no candidate exceeds this, the development protocol enters HOLD and a lightweight model path is considered.

layer_1_inner_cv.data: V1 training folds only, identity-level CV
layer_1_inner_cv.held_out: V1 OOF validation identities are never seen
layer_1_inner_cv.metrics_reported: AUROC, AUPRC, per-route, per-duration-bucket, first/later gap

layer_2_engineering_oof.purpose: locked engineering OOF on V1 validation identities
layer_2_engineering_oof.data: V1 validation identities (same folds as V1 OOF)
layer_2_engineering_oof.caveat: These identities indirectly informed V2 design through V1 failure analysis. Results are engineering evidence, not fully independent confirmation.
layer_2_engineering_oof.metrics_reported: all head/route/temporal/safety metrics + duration buckets + per-seed variance

layer_3_cal_check.data: CAL split (threshold selection) + untouched CHECK split (one-shot evaluation)
layer_3_cal_check.caveat: CHECK identities must not have been examined at any stage of V1 or V2 development
layer_3_cal_check.metrics_reported: frozen threshold recall, precision, safety emit rates, per-route, duration buckets

release_auroc.note: must exceed V1 0.72 by meaningful margin

short_event_recall_gap.note: V1 gap was 0.44; must narrow substantially

cal_check_minimum.note: Defined in final V2 protocol after architecture selected. Based on CAL threshold + untouched CHECK.

v2_success_criteria.no_v1_comparison_gaming: V2 must be evaluated under identical protocols. Cannot re-define metrics to make V1 look worse or V2 look better.

training_constraints.teacher_labels: V1 Factorized Teacher V1 labels UNCHANGED. No re-labeling, no window expansion.
training_constraints.identity_balancing: NEW: within each route, each identity contributes approximately equal weight to the loss. Implemented via per-identity loss normalization before route aggregation.
training_constraints.duration_balancing: NEW: within release loss, events are bucketed by duration [<15, 15-30, 30-50, 50-100, 100+]. Each bucket contributes equal weight to the total release loss.

data_augmentation.temporal_jitter: During training only: randomly offset the causal window by ±4 steps. The prediction target remains at the original step. This prevents the model from learning fixed step offsets within events.
data_augmentation.identity_resampling: During training only: with probability 0.5, replace an episode with another episode of the same route from the same fold. This reduces identity-specific memorization.
forbidden: any augmentation that uses future information

next_step: Inner-CV execution on V2 candidates. After selection, freeze final V2 protocol with locked architecture and hyperparameters.
